articles.title: Infant feeding practices may influence the timing of puberty in girls
articles.summary: A large observational study indicates that girls fed human milk as infants tend to experience a later onset of puberty compared to those fed exclusively with infant formula, highlighting potential long-term effects of early childhood nutrition.

articles.title: Stress hormones drive female-specific brain rewiring following ketamine anesthesia
articles.summary: A new study reveals that female mice experience a surge in stress hormones after ketamine anesthesia, prompting immune cells to rewire the brain. The findings highlight profound sex differences in how the brain recovers from anesthetics.

articles.title: How monogamous and polyamorous individuals envision multiple romantic partners
articles.summary: When asked to design two ideal romantic partners, most people prefer two well-rounded matches. However, differences emerge when people plan to invest their time and resources unequally between relationships, revealing how structure shapes human mating preferences.

articles.title: Researchers identify a simple way to soften deep political divides
articles.summary: People often overestimate how much their political opponents despise them. But new research suggests that tweaking your daily news diet could help correct these toxic assumptions and unexpectedly foster a sense of connection with the other side.

articles.title: HEPA air purifiers may boost brain function after just one month
articles.summary: Adults aged 40 and older performed about 12% faster on a test of executive function after using a HEPA air purifier at home for one month. The findings suggest that cleaner indoor air could offer a simple way to help protect the brain from the effects of traffic-related pollution.

articles.title: Scientists challenge a 70-year-old “lizard brain” myth
articles.summary: A long-standing picture of brain evolution as newer, rational layers stacked on top of an ancient “lizard brain” may be deeply misleading. Researchers found that evolution instead appears to balance two competing styles of brain wiring, expanding one while shrinking the other depending on what an animal needs to survive.

articles.title: Researchers followed 400,000 kids for 20 years and found a lasting pre-K advantage
articles.summary: A 20-year study of 400,000 students found that children who attended public school pre-K earned better grades and test scores through high school than those in other childcare settings. Better-trained teachers and earlier exposure to structured classrooms may help explain why the advantage lasted so long.

articles.title: Time Capsule of Testable Human Knowledge: 41 Years of Jeopardy! in a Single Free Local Model
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.27459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2011, IBM's Watson was something like a sealed capsule of its era's queryable knowledge. Its DeepQA system defeated the strongest human Jeopardy! champions, but the knowledge that let it do so lived in a curated billion-document corpus running on a cluster of POWER7 servers, frozen at build time and impossible to move or copy. We show that the same kind of artifact, a snapshot of what a culture can answer, is now portable and essentially free. We evaluate a single 9 GB open-weight model (Qwen2.5-14B, 4-bit) against the complete open Jeopardy!

articles.title: Rating the Raters: Rasch Measurement Theory for LLM Evaluation
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.27463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs now sit on every side of evaluation: as examinees scored on benchmarks, judges of other models' outputs, and raters of human-generated content. Each paradigm can be viewed as a measurement problem, where a latent property of an object is probed with items from an instrument (e.g., benchmark) by raters. articles.title: Marginal Coverage Credit Reduces Redundant Exploration in Parallel State-Entropy Optimization
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.27507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy Gradient for Parallel State Entropy maximization (PGPSE) expands state-space coverage by training independently parameterized policies in replicated copies of the same environment. However, its pooled team-entropy score measures only collective exploration and cannot identify policies that contribute non-redundant coverage. We introduce Marginal Coverage Credit for PGPSE (MCC-PGPSE), which combines leave-one-policy-out coverage with state-owner specialization to estimate policy-specific credit. MCC-PGPSE preserves PGPSE's pooled objective

articles.title: Quantization-Triggered Backdoors in Language Models: Cross-Quantizer Transferability and the Validation--Deployment Gap
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.27512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training quantization is often treated as a semantically neutral optimization for edge deployment of Large Language Models. When a full-precision source checkpoint is evaluated and quantization is applied downstream without equivalent re-evaluation, this workflow creates a structural validation--deployment gap: because quantization is a many-to-one mapping over parameter space, source-precision certification does not guarantee behavioral equivalence in the deployed configuration. We formalize this gap through Quantization Behavioral Equivale
